reviews.review: It's not the worst Psuedo-L4D but god the really stiff animations and not very punchy weapon sounds drag it down a lot.  No real bullet penetration also does make shotgun weapons feel terrible, honestly all the weapons feel really boring for the setting we're given.
It needs some polishing (but which version 1.0 doesn't), but is a fun horde PvE shooter.

There's a joker with a review on here complaining about the startup achievement having 0.0% of players... bud the non-Barry related achievements were added on the 1.0 release, presumably hours before he played the game. This may come as a shock, but steam achievement statistics do not, in fact, update in real time.

As for the actual game review, it's a L4D clone, with all that entails including the versus mode. I like the lineup of special enemies, especially the spawner with its rolling turrets and the odd spiky balls. The flasher is also imo a good idea, as he can make it difficult to see what you are aiming at or get a sense of direction at critical moments. I get why it's not a popular enemy, but there's an option to reduce the effect for people who dislike it. 

I will say the game quality is reduced pretty dramatically with the later episodes. Episode 5 in particular is upsetting because it's only 20 minutes long. The concept is that it's a low commitment versus map but my group doesn't really care about that. What's regrettable is they added a bunch of banter for this level that I wish they had more of for the rest of the game, and the map quality is consistently high throughout the game, so the final level being so short and the ending being essentially nonexistent really hurt. I assume this is because they were running out of money and the playerbase and sales numbers couldn't support it. I also miss the early access feature where weapons had different variants that would spawn; my group liked this a lot as it made each weapon discovery feel important.

That said, a single playthrough on normal is about 6 hours for the average group, and the earlier episodes are excellent. The retrofuture aesthetic and the enemy variety along with the roguelike-style upgrades make the game stand out enough to be worth playing. My friends and I liked it enough to go through a second time despite having a long queue of games to get to. If you're looking for something L4D adjacent this is a good pick.

I've been playing The Anacrusis every few months from EA launch up to now, and each play session I've been astounded at how much love and joy has gone into the game. The 1.0 release though was head and shoulders above the rest - absolutely gorgeous presentation and dialled in UX.

Wishing there were more folk online, but adored the interactions I've had the past week since 1.0 shipped. Looking forward to playing a squad of 4 this weekend!
Has a lot of potential, and some of the set pieces look beautiful. But there's literally no one playing.

The bones are there for a really solid replacement for L4D, with all the mod trappings of the OG source implementations. Mods are universal and networked, there's a full level SDK for level designers. There's still some slight hangups, netcode makes enemy movement feel a bit spongey, there's some visual weirdness on shooting enemies / when they actually died, but the core gameplay, level design and campaign mechanics are a blast to play through if you can look past those shortfalls.
